name: slice-story
context_rationale: Inline orchestrator: resolves the active slice folder, spawns the forked slice-story narrator subagent for the heavy plain-language synthesis (keeping the parent context lean), then renders the returned JSON to story.html via render_story.py and performs an OUTWARD side-effect — uploading the report to Google Drive via the Google Drive MCP tool — and ends by prompting the user to run /build-slice. The outward push + the user prompt + the slice-folder write all need the parent conversation's tool access and authority, so the orchestrator stays main-agent and only the narration is forked.
summary: Turns one slice's internal artifacts into a single plain-language STORY for a mixed technical / non-technical audience (tilted slightly technical, zero pipeline jargon), rendered as a standalone story.html. Adaptive across the lifecycle: before building it tells the objective, what was proven in spikes, how it's built, and what the design review changed; after building it adds what was built, what code review found, what reality testing showed, and what was learned. A forked slice-story narrator subagent reads the artifacts and returns structured JSON; render_story.py renders the HTML deterministically; the report is saved in the slice folder AND pushed to Google Drive; then the user is asked to start /build-slice when ready. Runs just after /critique (the pre-build report) and is also user-invokable any time. Never modifies source files.

agents.name: slice-story
agents.when: After the active slice folder is resolved — before rendering/upload
agents.purpose: Forked narrator: reads the slice artifacts handed to it, translates every pipeline code into plain English, and returns the slice STORY as structured story-sections JSON (no file writes, no HTML) so the heavy synthesis stays out of the parent context

methodology_tools.name: render_story
methodology_tools.purpose: Deterministic, dependency-free renderer: turns the narrator's story-sections.json into a self-contained, styled, print-friendly story.html (inline CSS, no JS, no external assets). Single-skill script; owns all styling so the look is consistent and the agent never hand-writes HTML.

harness_tools.name: Read
harness_tools.purpose: Read the active slice artifacts (mission-brief.json, design.json, spikes, ADRs, critique.json, critique-review.json, and any post-build build-log/code-review/validation/reflection) to hand to the narrator; read story.html back for the Google Drive upload

harness_tools.name: Write
harness_tools.purpose: Write the narrator's returned story-sections.json into the slice folder before rendering

harness_tools.name: Bash
harness_tools.purpose: Resolve the active slice folder + lifecycle stage (live-state injection) and run render_story.py

harness_tools.name: Agent
harness_tools.purpose: Spawn the named slice-story narrator subagent (subagent_type: slice-story) for the forked plain-language synthesis

harness_tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Google_Drive__create_file
harness_tools.purpose: Upload story.html to Google Drive (text/html, conversion disabled) and return the shareable link; degrades gracefully with a local-only note if the Drive MCP server is not connected

file_access.purpose: The slice intent, acceptance criteria, must-not-defer, out-of-scope — the front of the story
Components, interfaces, data deltas, auth + error handling — the 'how it's built' section
Risk-spike verdicts — the 'what we proved before building' section (read when present)
Decisions locked by this slice, with reversibility — the 'decisions we locked' section
Reviewer findings + what the team decided — the 'what the review changed' section
Second-pass review (missed/over-flagged items) folded into the review-changes narrative when present
Determine the furthest lifecycle stage reached, to decide which sections the story includes
Post-build: what was actually built, deferrals, deviations — the 'what we built' section (read when present)
Post-build: code-review findings in plain language — the 'what the code review found' section (read when present)
Post-build: reality-test results — the 'what reality testing showed' section (read when present)
Post-build: what held up, what was wrong, what we'd change — the 'what we learned' section (read when present)

The narrator's structured story (the render input); persisted so story.html can be re-rendered without re-running the agent. Per-slice active-folder artifact — raw-write is correct (not a shared aggregate).
The deliverable: a standalone, self-contained plain-language report of the slice, saved in the slice folder and uploaded to Google Drive

Outward push of story.html to the user's Google Drive via the Drive MCP create_file tool (text/html, conversion disabled); returns a shareable link. Skipped gracefully if the Drive MCP server is not connected.
